title: How Atomic Clocks Define the Second

post_description: How cesium atoms define the second and why atomic clocks are so accurate, from NIST and NASA. Sources: National Institute of Standards and Technology https://www.nist.gov/how-do-you-measure-it/how-do-you-measure-second and National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://www.nasa.gov/missions/tech-demonstration/deep-space-atomic-clock/what-is-an-atomic-clock/ #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: How do we measure a single second so precisely? Atomic clocks are the most accurate way to measure time. Inside, waves are aimed at cesium atoms, and the atoms absorb them and leap to a different energy level. That jump only happens at one precise frequency. Cesium atoms respond to one exact, steady count of wave cycles, so the second itself is defined by counting those cycles. The best cesium clocks drift by only a tiny fraction of a second each year. A quartz wristwatch may be off by several seconds a month. Quartz clocks drift too: after six weeks, even good ones can be off by a full millisecond.
